name: LIC Housing Finance Ltd.
business_summary: Housing finance company (NHB/RBI regulated) promoted by LIC (45.24%), financing individual home purchase/construction (97% retail book in H1 FY27), plus LAP, developer/project finance and LRD. Portfolio ~Rs 3 lakh cr; funded mainly by NCDs and bank borrowings. Q2 FY27 PAT ~Rs 1,507 cr (+11% y/y); Stage 3 2.05%; Rs 553 cr retail recoveries; mgmt targets 14-15% disbursement growth. Trades at 0.65x book and ~4.9x earnings.

cost_structure.note: interest Rs 19.7k cr of Rs 28.6k cr revenue

exposures.mechanism: +25bp repo: Morgan Stanley estimates +7.2% PBT (7 Oct 2026) because asset book is largely floating (LIC HFL PLR-linked) and reprices faster than market borrowings (NCD ~50%, bank ~20-25%, deposits/NHB rest - model knowledge). PBT +7.2% x persistence 0.5 -> ~+3.6; haircut for higher discount rate and spread-compression risk -> +3.0, range -2..+6. Empirical Fed funds +4.43/SSU (t 2.9) is a rate-cycle co-movement, agrees in sign.

evidence.note: Morgan Stanley sees 7.2% PBT boost for LIC HFL from 25bp repo hike (Business Upturn headline)

exposures.mechanism: ~85% of borrowings are market-linked; interest Rs 19.7k cr TTM. +50bp on ~Rs 2.7 lakh cr liabilities with ~40% repricing in a year = Rs 540 cr vs financing profit Rs 7.6k cr = -7%; pass-through 40% -> -4.3%; persistence 0.5 -> -3.
+25bp G-sec lifts NCD pricing (bond market benchmark) and the P/B discount rate; lender trades at 0.65x book so downside to multiple limited; -1.5.

+10% housing sales -> disbursement growth +3pp (mgmt targets 14-15% growth, Q2 disbursements +11%) -> AUM +1pp -> NII +1.5%; leverage on 97% retail book; persistence 0.7 -> +1.0; plus spread-stability effect -> +2.

evidence.note: Rs 553 cr recoveries from retail portfolio; targets 14-15% disbursement growth (Livemint)

exposures.mechanism: Credit cost currently ~0.2-0.3% (Stage 3 2.05%, Rs 553 cr retail recoveries in Q2). +50bp on ~Rs 3 lakh cr book = Rs 1.5k cr = -19% of Rs 7.6k cr financing profit; persistence 0.4 -> -7.6; asymmetry because developer exposure and the Essel/Subhash Chandra-guarantee loans (four firms offering full repayment, 8 Oct) are legacy stress points.

evidence.note: Q2 PAT up 11% (BusinessLine; headline prints Rs 150.7 cr, likely Rs 1,507 cr per screener); Stage 3 2.05%
Four firms offer full repayment on loans backed by Subhash Chandra guarantee (Millennium Post)

exposures.mechanism: Banks' deposit growth keeps competing bank housing loans cheap (bank home-loan rates 7.1-7.35%, Upstox 7 Oct) - competition narrows LIC HFL's spread; ambiguous, tiny positive via system liquidity.
Interest subvention, PMAY-U 2.0, Sec 24/80EEA tax changes raise affordable-home demand: +1 step -> disbursements +3% -> ~+2.5; LIC HFL has Tier-2/3 affordable mix.
NHB/RBI scale-based HFC regulation (risk weights, LTV, project-finance provisioning) tightening raises provisions and capital need; -2 expected.
+3pp system credit growth: housing credit grows faster in expansions; LIC HFL market share declining (portfolio growth ~7-8%). +1.5.
Empirical +4.43/SSU t=2.9 over 3y reflects a rate-cycle regime where rising rates coincided with HFC NIM expansion; judged partly coincidental and shrunk to +1.0.
FIIs fell 21.47% -> 18.93% (Jun -> Sep 2026); beta 1.39; flow reversal would unwind some of the pressure.

company_links.mechanism: Per +10% move in LICI equity value: LIC holds 45.24% (promoter); sentiment link on LIC deal flow/support and parent-brand sentiment; reverse link is the scale effect. +1.0 per +10% (assumed unit: % equity of dst per +10% of src).

supply_chain.counterparty: HDFC Bank / SBI / Bajaj Housing Finance
supply_chain.note: prime home loans compete on rates (7.1-7.35% bank offers)

company_events.event: Q3 FY27 results (Q2 was 30 Oct 2026; Q3 likely late Jan/early Feb)
RBI MPC December: further hike would help HFC NIM near-term but hurt demand
Resolution of Essel/Subhash Chandra-guarantee exposures (full repayment offers noted 8 Oct)

current_state.trend: Profit +11% y/y; H1 spreads narrowed as lending yield fell faster than cost of funds (Multibagg AI); Stage 3 2.05% but coverage dropped; disbursements +11%
current_state.valuation: P/E 4.9, P/B 0.65, dividend yield 1.9%; deep discount to Bajaj/HDFC peers; analysts Hold (target Rs 520, ICICI Sec and Prabhudas Lilladher, 3 Nov)
recent_developments: 2026-10-07: RBI hikes repo; Morgan Stanley sees +7.2% PBT for LIC HFL
2026-10-08: four firms offer full repayment on Subhash Chandra-guaranteed loans
2026-11-01: mgmt sees double-digit growth in H2, portfolio to ~Rs 3.5 lakh cr (BusinessLine)
2026-11-03: Rs 553 cr recoveries; targets 14-15% disbursement growth; brokerages Hold

key_risks: Spread compression from competitive prime pricing and lower lending yields
Stage 3 coverage decline and legacy developer / guarantee exposures
Wholesale funding cost if spreads widen
Slower housing demand if rate hikes persist
upside_triggers: Rate-hike NIM benefit (PLR resets before liabilities)
